primary_diagnosis_treated: Metabolic syndrome (essential hypertension, dyslipidaemia, prediabetes, obesity)

medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line for hypertension; NICE NG107 recommends ACE‑I for CKD renoprotection

medications.dose: 5 mg once daily; increase to 10 mg after 4 weeks if BP >140/90 mmHg
medications.duration: Lifelong – review every 4–6 weeks during titration then annually
medications.purpose: Add‑on antihypertensive to achieve target BP <140/90 mmHg
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends a CCB as second‑line when BP remains uncontrolled on ACE‑I/ARB

medications.duration: Lifelong – review lipid profile at 12 weeks, titrate to 40 mg if LDL target not met
medications.purpose: Reduce LDL and cardiovascular risk in metabolic syndrome
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181/PH46 advise statin therapy for LDL >100 mg/dL or QRISK ≥10%

medications.dose: 500 mg orally nightly; increase to 500 mg twice daily after 1 week, then 1 g twice daily after another week as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong – review HbA1c and renal function every 3–6 months
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 recommends metformin for high‑risk prediabetes with BMI ≥30 kg/m² when eGFR ≥30

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive antihypertensive effect; risk of symptomatic hypotension and peripheral oedema
interactions_checked.action: Monitor blood pressure and for peripheral oedema after dose increase; counsel patient to report swelling

interactions_checked.interaction: No direct interaction; both renally cleared – monitor renal function
interactions_checked.action: Check eGFR before initiation and periodically thereafter

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥45 mL/min/1.73 m² based on creatinine 1.3 mg/dL for a middle‑aged male; will obtain eGFR before starting metformin or up‑titrating lisinopril.
Baseline liver function tests not available – required before initiating atorvastatin and for monitoring.
QRISK score not calculated – needed to confirm cardiovascular risk justification for statin; assumed high given risk profile.
Allergy status unknown – will verify no hypersensitivity to ACE‑I, CCB, statin, or metformin.
Serum potassium is high‑normal (5.0 mmol/L); avoid adding potassium‑raising agents and monitor potassium after any dose change.
treatment_summary: The plan addresses metabolic syndrome by optimizing blood pressure with amlodipine add‑on to existing lisinopril, initiating atorvastatin for dyslipidaemia, and starting metformin MR for prediabetes, all supported by NICE guidelines. Baseline labs (eGFR, LFTs, QRISK) are required before initiation, and regular monitoring of BP, lipids, glucose, renal function, and potassium is outlined.
